mainEntity.name: When should I repair my tile roof versus replacing it entirely?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deciding between repair and replacement depends on the extent of the damage and the roof's overall condition. If only a few tiles are damaged, or a small area is leaking, repair is usually sufficient and more cost-effective. However, if there's widespread damage, multiple leaks, or the roof is nearing the end of its lifespan (typically 50-100 years for tile), a full replacement might be the better long-term investment. A professional inspection can help determine if the existing issues are isolated or indicative of systemic wear.
acceptedAnswer.description: Repair if damage is localized; replace if there's widespread damage, multiple leaks, or the roof is at the end of its lifespan. A professional can help assess the best option.
